headline: Strikes spread along the Gdansk coast
summary: By August 16, 1980, the strike that began at Gdansk's Lenin Shipyard two days earlier had spread to other shipyards and to municipal transport along the coast. Delegates from the striking enterprises formed an Inter-Factory Strike Committee under Lech Walesa, which drew up the workers' twenty-one demands.
significance: The committee turned a shipyard dispute into a regional movement with political demands, above all the right to free trade unions. Its agreement with the government on August 31 led to Solidarity.
fbis: The East Europe report of August 18, 1980, carried Gdansk radio's report of August 16 acknowledging work stoppages in shipyards and municipal transport along the coast, framed as demands over pay and conditions, with reassurance that trains ran and the shops were supplied.
